---
title: "Tutorial 5 — Self-check answers"
sidebar: mfml
---

1. Type I: predict positive when negative (false positive). Type II: predict negative when positive (false negative).  
2. Type I $\le\alpha$; among all such rules, minimize type II (maximize true-positive rate).  
3. Likelihood-ratio test vs threshold $K$; $K$ is chosen so type I equals $\alpha$.  
4. Both need the ratio of class-conditional densities $p(x\mid Y=1)/p(x\mid Y=0)$.  
5. Type II error typically increases (harder to declare positive).
